南锣鼓巷位于北京鼓楼与地安门之间，南北向，全长786米，宽约8米。所附资料称其与.en: Nanluoguxiang is located between Beijing Drum Tower and Di’anmen, running north–south, with a total length of 786 meters and a width of approximately 8 meters. The accompanying materials state that it took shape during the same period as Dadu of the Yuan dynasty. Sixteen branch lanes line both sides of the street, which retains an overall checkerboard-style neighborhood layout as well as the traditional hutong and courtyard pattern. The materials also record that the lane was formerly called “Luoguoxiang” and was renamed Nanluoguxiang in the 1750 Complete Map of the City. The existing materials describe both the character of the historic district and its later commercial and leisure activities.

福祥胡同是南锣鼓巷西侧八条支巷之一，位于传统胡同片区内。2020年东城区相关报道.en: Fuxiang Hutong is one of the eight branch lanes on the west side of Nanluoguxiang, within a traditional hutong area. A 2020 report concerning Dongcheng District included it in the scope of renovation and restoration, stating that the hutong pattern and courtyard character were retained after the work, while residents’ housing, kitchen and bathroom facilities, and municipal infrastructure were improved. The existing materials focus on the overall renewal of the lane and residents’ living environment and do not provide Fuxiang Hutong’s individual length, width, or a specific list of historic buildings.

蓑衣胡同是南锣鼓巷西侧支巷之一。东城区融媒体转引的报道显示，蓑衣胡同与雨儿、帽儿.en: Suoyi Hutong is one of the branch lanes on the west side of Nanluoguxiang. A report reproduced by Dongcheng District’s integrated media states that Suoyi Hutong, Yuer Hutong, Mao’er Hutong, and Fuxiang Hutong underwent renovation and improvement together. The project emphasized retaining the original hutong pattern and courtyard character while improving residents’ living conditions and the public environment. The accompanying materials do not provide Suoyi Hutong’s individual historical development, dimensions, or a list of courtyards.

雨儿胡同是南锣鼓巷西侧支巷之一。现有报道记载，该胡同在整治修缮中保留胡同肌理和院.en: Yuer Hutong is one of the branch lanes on the west side of Nanluoguxiang. Existing reports record that the hutong’s pattern and courtyard character were retained during renovation and improvement, while residents’ housing, municipal facilities, and the public environment were improved. The reports specifically introduce Courtyard No. 30, formerly the site of a storeroom of the Qing dynasty banner office responsible for annual duty. Some vacated rooms were later converted into spaces for residents’ discussions, public activities, community services, and exhibitions. The materials also state that Qi Baishi once lived at No. 13 Yuer Hutong.

帽儿胡同位于北京老城区鼓楼与地安门之间，东西向，全长565米、宽7米。首都之窗资.en: Mao’er Hutong is located between the Drum Tower and Di’anmen in Beijing’s old city, running east–west, with a total length of 565 meters and a width of 7 meters. Materials from the Capital Window state that it was already called Mao’er Hutong during the Qianlong period of the Qing dynasty. The name has continued to the present; it was temporarily changed to Fourth Huihuang Street before being restored. The hutong contains historic residences and gardens including Keyuan and Courtyards Nos. 35 and 37. Keyuan was formerly the residence and garden of Wenyu, while Courtyards Nos. 35 and 37 once belonged to Wanrong’s maternal family. Existing materials emphasize that the gates of these residences can only be viewed from outside and do not state that their interiors are regularly open.

景阳胡同被所附北京旅游网资料列为南锣鼓巷西侧八条支巷之一。现有来源未提供该胡同单.en: Jingyang Hutong is listed in the accompanying Beijing Tourism materials as one of the eight branch lanes on the west side of Nanluoguxiang. Existing sources provide no separate information on the hutong’s length, width, historical development of its name, building inventory, or renovation details. Its identity within the traditional branch-lane system of Nanluoguxiang can therefore be confirmed, but its specific history cannot be supplemented with information about the broader historic district.

沙井胡同被所附北京旅游网资料列为南锣鼓巷西侧八条支巷之一。现有来源没有提供沙井胡.en: Shajing Hutong is listed in the accompanying Beijing Tourism materials as one of the eight branch lanes on the west side of Nanluoguxiang. Existing sources provide no separate information on its dimensions, changes in name, historic buildings, or renovation. This entry therefore only confirms, on the basis of the sources, that it belongs to the Nanluoguxiang branch-lane system and does not transfer information from the broader historic district or other hutongs.

黑芝麻胡同是南锣鼓巷西侧八条支巷之一。所附资料还记载，黑芝麻胡同2号曾有“烧肉人.en: Heizhima Hutong is one of the eight branch lanes on the west side of Nanluoguxiang. The accompanying materials also record that No. 2 Heizhima Hutong once housed the “Shaorouren” roast-meat restaurant; No. 59 was formerly the residence of Hong Chengchou, a general who defected to the Qing at the end of the Ming dynasty; and No. 13 was once the residence of Kui Jun, a Minister of the Board of Punishments in the Qing dynasty. These details show that the source presents the hutong as a fragment where traditional streets, historic residences, and commercial activities coexist, but it does not provide the length, width, or uniform access information for the entire hutong.

前鼓楼苑胡同是南锣鼓巷东、西两侧支巷体系中西侧的八条胡同之一。所给官方正文按由南.en: Qian Gulouyuan Hutong is one of the eight hutongs on the west side of the east-and-west branch-lane system of Nanluoguxiang. The official text provided lists its name in south-to-north order but gives no further information on its historical development, length, buildings, or specific courtyards.

炒豆胡同是南锣鼓巷东侧八条胡同之一。官方正文特别记载，炒豆胡同77号原为清代僧格.en: Chaodou Hutong is one of the eight hutongs on the east side of Nanluoguxiang. The official text specifically records that No. 77 Chaodou Hutong was formerly the residence of Prince Senggelinqin of the Qing dynasty, with its front gate on Chaodou Hutong and rear gate on Banchang Hutong. The family ancestral shrine of Senggelinqin was also located at its western entrance. These accounts are historical materials and cannot be used to determine its present condition or access.

板厂胡同是南锣鼓巷东侧八条胡同之一。所给正文还记载，清代僧格林沁王府的后门在板厂.en: Banchang Hutong is one of the eight hutongs on the east side of Nanluoguxiang. The text provided also records that the rear gate of Prince Senggelinqin’s residence in the Qing dynasty was on Banchang Hutong, but gives no further information on the formation, length, street pattern, or surviving buildings of Banchang Hutong itself. This historical association does not mean that the entire hutong consists of remains of the princely residence.

东棉花胡同是南锣鼓巷东侧八条胡同之一。正文记载，东棉花胡同39号现为中央戏剧学院.en: Dongmianhua Hutong is one of the eight hutongs on the east side of Nanluoguxiang. The text records that No. 39 Dongmianhua Hutong is now the Central Academy of Drama and was formerly the residence of Jin Yunpeng. The source also states that part of the Jin residence’s courtyard compound was converted into Western-style buildings and that the old buildings were later completely demolished. These details concern a specific address and do not represent the entire hutong.

北兵马司胡同是南锣鼓巷东侧八条胡同之一。所给官方正文仅将其列入由南向北的胡同名录.en: Beibingmasi Hutong is one of the eight hutongs on the east side of Nanluoguxiang. The official text provided only lists it in the south-to-north register of hutongs and gives no information specific to it concerning the origin of its name, historical figures, architectural remains, length, or other matters. At present, its identity as a branch lane of Nanluoguxiang can only be confirmed; further individual facts cannot be added on this basis.

秦老胡同是南锣鼓巷东侧八条胡同之一。官方正文另记秦老胡同35号曾是清内务府总管大.en: Qinlao Hutong is one of the eight hutongs on the east side of Nanluoguxiang. The official text additionally records that No. 35 Qinlao Hutong was once the residence of the Suo family, headed by a Grand Minister of the Imperial Household Department in the Qing dynasty. It does not describe the current condition of the residence or extend the history of this address to the entire hutong. Apart from its place in the name sequence and this historical association, the source provides no further information specific to it.

前圆恩寺胡同是南锣鼓巷东侧八条胡同之一。现有官方正文在胡同名录中确认了这一名称，.en: Qianyuan’en Temple Hutong is one of the eight hutongs on the east side of Nanluoguxiang. Existing official text confirms this name in the register of hutongs but provides no information on its historical development, length, street form, or specific courtyards. The available information is insufficient to determine the hutong’s degree of preservation, current use, or visiting conditions.

后圆恩寺胡同是南锣鼓巷东侧八条胡同之一。正文记载，后圆恩寺胡同13号为茅盾故居，.en: Houyuan’en Temple Hutong is one of the eight hutongs on the east side of Nanluoguxiang. The text records that No. 13 Houyuan’en Temple Hutong is the former residence of Mao Dun, with the rear courtyard arranged according to its original appearance during his lifetime. No. 7 was once Chiang Kai-shek’s headquarters in Beiping; the building was originally the residence of the Qing imperial clansman Zai Fu. These are historical details concerning specific addresses and cannot be generalized to the entire hutong.

菊儿胡同位于南锣鼓巷东侧，名称沿革可追溯至明代“局儿胡同”，后曾称“橘儿胡同”，.en: Ju’er Hutong is located east of Nanluoguxiang. The historical development of its name can be traced to “Juer Hutong” in the Ming dynasty; it was later called “Juer Hutong” with a different character, and the present name was established during the Xuantong period of the Qing dynasty. In 1990, Wu Liangyong led the renovation of dilapidated housing and addressed the traditional hutong residential environment through “organic renewal,” allowing it to retain the character of old Beijing courtyard residences while meeting modern residential needs. Public materials also record that the project received the Asian Architecture Gold Award in 1992 and the World Habitat Award in 1993. Ju’er Hutong remains a residential living space, and the materials do not state that courtyard interiors are generally open.

僧王府，即僧格林沁王府，是一处跨炒豆胡同、南锣鼓巷和板厂胡同的府址。北京市文物局.en: The Prince Seng Residence, namely Prince Senggelinqin’s residence, is a princely compound extending across Chaodou Hutong, Nanluoguxiang, and Banchang Hutong. The protection area announced by the Beijing Municipal Cultural Heritage Bureau includes the existing enclosing walls of Courtyards Nos. 75 and 77 Chaodou Hutong, the south-central and north courtyards of No. 110 Nanluoguxiang, and Courtyards Nos. 30, 32, and 34 Banchang Hutong. Another official historical text states that the residence was large, with its front gate on Chaodou Hutong and rear gate on Banchang Hutong. It also records that Senggelinqin died in battle at Caozhou, Shandong, in 1865. After his son inherited the title of Prince, the site was also known popularly as the “Residence of Prince Bo.”

僧格林沁祠堂旧址据官方文旅旧文记载，位于炒豆胡同西口，是僧格林沁家族祠堂。该文同.en: According to an official historical cultural-tourism text, the former site of the Senggelinqin Ancestral Shrine was located at the western entrance of Chaodou Hutong and was the ancestral shrine of the Senggelinqin family. The text also states that the shrine and the Prince Seng Residence were built on the same hutong, describing this as an unusual layout in Beijing. Existing materials provide only its historical relationship with the princely compound and its approximate location, without an independent designation number as a protected cultural heritage site, a specific address, information on the preservation of the buildings, or current access arrangements. This entry therefore only identifies the historical site.

可园及文煜宅是帽儿胡同内相连的一组宅院与园林。北京市文物局公布的保护范围将可园列.en: Keyuan and the Wenyu Residence are a connected group of residences and gardens in Mao’er Hutong. The protection area announced by the Beijing Municipal Cultural Heritage Bureau lists Keyuan as Courtyards Nos. 7, 9, 11, and 13 Mao’er Hutong, and separately lists the Courtyards Nos. 3 and 5 of No. 5 Mao’er Hutong in Dongcheng District. The official introduction states that Nos. 7–15 Mao’er Hutong were formerly the residence and garden of Wenyu, a Grand Secretary in the Qing dynasty, and that Keyuan was modeled on Suzhou’s Humble Administrator’s Garden and Lion Grove Garden. The materials also record that the garden residence later belonged to Feng Guozhang and was used for a period as the Embassy of the Republic of Korea in China.

婉容故居位于帽儿胡同35、37号院，官方资料称这里是清朝末代皇后婉容的娘家，俗称.en: Wanrong’s Former Residence is located at Courtyards Nos. 35 and 37 Mao’er Hutong. Official materials state that it was the maternal family home of Wanrong, the last empress of the Qing dynasty, and was commonly known as the “Empress’s Residence.” They also record that Wanrong was born here in 1906. After she was installed as empress, the residence underwent extensive renovation. It later became the home of the scholar Zhu Jiajin and is now a Beijing Municipal Protected Cultural Heritage Site. Public materials specifically state that today the main view is of the exterior of the residence and its gate, and this does not establish that the private courtyards or interiors are open to the public.

齐白石旧居纪念馆位于北京市东城区雨儿胡同13号院，是一座清中期四合院建筑，官方资.en: The Qi Baishi Former Residence Memorial Museum is located at Courtyard No. 13 Yuer Hutong, Dongcheng District, Beijing. It is a mid-Qing dynasty courtyard residence, which official materials identify as a protected cultural heritage site of Dongcheng District. In 1955, under the care of Zhou Enlai, the state Ministry of Culture allocated funds to purchase it and made it available to Qi Baishi as a residence. Qi Baishi created a number of important works here in his later years. The memorial museum has been reconstructed according to his living and working conditions in his later years, presenting the courtyard environment and the artist’s residential and creative life. The materials do not provide current access arrangements in this entry.

茅盾故居位于北京市东城区交道口后圆恩寺胡同13号，占地面积878平方米。茅盾于1.en: Mao Dun’s Former Residence is located at No. 13 Houyuan’en Temple Hutong, Jiaodaokou, Dongcheng District, Beijing, occupying an area of 878 square meters. Mao Dun lived here from 1974 to 1981. The sitting room and reception room in the residence retain their original appearance, and materials including books, daily articles, clothing, stationery, and identification documents from his lifetime are displayed. Public information from the Beijing Municipal Government records that Mao Dun’s Former Residence was announced as a Beijing Municipal Protected Cultural Heritage Site on May 24, 1984. Another official historical text also states that the bedroom and study in the rear courtyard were arranged according to their original appearance during his lifetime.

蒋介石北平行辕旧址即后圆恩寺胡同7号宅院，官方旧文称其原为清宗室载旉宅第，建筑坐.en: The former site of Chiang Kai-shek’s Beiping headquarters is the residence at No. 7 Houyuan’en Temple Hutong. An official historical text states that it was originally the residence of the Qing imperial clansman Zai Fu, with the building facing south and featuring a combination of Chinese and Western characteristics. After the victory of the War of Resistance, the materials record that the residence served as Chiang Kai-shek’s headquarters in Beiping from December 1945 to January 1949. During this period he visited Beiping to express concern for compatriots in the north, and in September 1948 dealt with the Liaoshen Campaign there. Another official historical text states that after 1948 the compound received a new occupant, the “Office of the Central Committee’s North China Bureau.” These are historical uses and do not indicate its current access status.
蒋介石北平行辕旧址即后圆恩寺胡同7号宅院，官方旧文称其原为清宗室载旉宅第，建筑坐.revision: Codex依给定中文作专名、方位、混字及铭文转写的确定性校正；无新增模型调用

文旅旧文将菊儿胡同3号、5号、7号及寿比胡同6号合称为清代直隶总督、兵部尚书荣禄.en: A historical cultural-tourism text groups Nos. 3, 5, and 7 Ju’er Hutong with No. 6 Shoubi Hutong as the residence of the father of Ronglu, a Governor-General of Zhili and Minister of War in the Qing dynasty. On this basis, the historical ownership of the residential group to which No. 7 Ju’er Hutong belongs can be identified. Existing sources do not describe the layout of the residence’s original garden, the specific condition of the buildings, or its current use.

秦老胡同35号据文旅旧文曾是清内务府总管大臣索家的府邸。现有材料仅能确认这一历史.en: According to a historical cultural-tourism text, No. 35 Qinlao Hutong was once the residence of the Suo family, headed by a Grand Minister of the Imperial Household Department in the Qing dynasty. Existing materials only confirm this historical association with the owner of the residence and provide no information on its architectural development, condition, current use, or interior access.

黑芝麻胡同13号据文旅旧文曾为清朝刑部尚书奎俊的宅邸。现有来源没有进一步说明宅院.en: According to a historical cultural-tourism text, No. 13 Heizhima Hutong was once the residence of Kui Jun, a Minister of the Board of Punishments in the Qing dynasty. Existing sources provide no further information on the residence’s construction date, layout, state of preservation, or present use. This entry therefore onlysummarizes the source’s record of its historical owner.
黑芝麻胡同13号据文旅旧文曾为清朝刑部尚书奎俊的宅邸。现有来源没有进一步说明宅院.revision: Codex依给定中文作专名、方位、混字及铭文转写的确定性校正；无新增模型调用

黑芝麻胡同59号的“洪承畴宅”身份，来自北京文旅旧文的历史记载。该文称此处原为明.en: The identification of No. 59 Heizhima Hutong as the “Hong Chengchou Residence” comes from a historical account in an old Beijing cultural-tourism text. The text states that it was formerly the residence of Hong Chengchou, a general who defected to the Qing at the end of the Ming dynasty, but does not explain the surviving buildings, changes in ownership, renovation, or access arrangements. This entry therefore only states the historical attribution recorded by the source.

沙井胡同15号四合院位于东城区南锣鼓巷地区，官方招标公告称其为传统老北京文物古建.en: The courtyard residence at No. 15 Shajing Hutong is located in the Nanluoguxiang area of Dongcheng District. An official tender announcement describes it as a traditional old-Beijing courtyard residence with historic cultural buildings. The compound was listed as a Beijing Municipal Protected Cultural Heritage Site in 2003 and occupies approximately 3,000 square meters. A 2015 announcement indicated that the relevant departments planned to implement lightning-protection works to strengthen management and eliminate safety hazards.

菊儿胡同新四合院改造项目由建筑大师吴良镛于1990年主持危房改造，文旅旧文概括为.en: The New Courtyard Residence Renovation Project at Ju’er Hutong was led by the architect Wu Liangyong in 1990 as a renovation of dilapidated housing. An old cultural-tourism text summarizes it as “organic renewal” of the hutong, adapting it to modern living while retaining the character of old Beijing courtyard residences. Materials from the Dongcheng District government state that the area still retains the character of a traditional residential district of Yuan-dynasty hutong courtyards. Existing materials do not specify the project boundaries, a list of individual buildings, or interior visiting arrangements.

东棉花胡同39号现为中央戏剧学院东城校区，文旅旧文记载这里原为靳云鹏旧宅，并称靳.en: No. 39 Dongmianhua Hutong is now the Dongcheng Campus of the Central Academy of Drama. An old cultural-tourism text records that it was formerly the residence of Jin Yunpeng and states that after purchasing it, Jin Yunpeng demolished part of the courtyard residences and built several Western-style buildings. The text further clearly records that the old buildings were later completely demolished and that no traces of the Jin residence remain. This object should therefore be understood as a record of a historic site and the development of a former residence.

什刹海是西城区北部的开放性风景区，由前海、后海、西海组成，水面约34万平方米。官.en: Shichahai is an open scenic area in northern Xicheng District, consisting of Qianhai, Houhai, and Xihai, with a water surface of approximately 340,000 square meters. Official historical and gazetteer materials record that its historical names included Bailiantan, Jishuitan, and Haizi. After water-conservancy improvements during the Yuan dynasty, it became an important water area connecting Dadu of the Yuan dynasty with the Beijing–Hangzhou Grand Canal. Cultural-tourism materials further include the scenic spots, historic sites, and residences along its banks within the present-day scenic area and describe it as one of Beijing’s first historic and cultural conservation areas.

前海是什刹海三片水域之一，属于开放性风景区的组成部分。资料将其置于高梁河水系及元.en: Qianhai is one of the three water areas of Shichahai and forms part of the open scenic area. The materials place it within the historical context of the Gaoliang River water system and the grain-transport system of Dadu of the Yuan dynasty. They record that after the founding of the People’s Republic of China, dredging, embankment construction, green-space creation, and other improvements were carried out. After renovation in the 1980s, lotus flowers were planted in Qianhai, and waterfront features including Tanyuan Shuiyuan, an island pavilion, fountains, and teahouses were developed.

后海是什刹海后三海之一，与前海、西海共同构成什刹海水域。官方旧文记载，后海北岸、.en: Houhai is one of the three rear seas of Shichahai and, together with Qianhai and Xihai, forms the waters of Shichahai. An official historical text records that the northern and eastern shores of Houhai were important areas of urban activity from the Yuan dynasty onward. After the founding of the People’s Republic of China, the waters and shores underwent dredging, embankment construction, green-space development, and environmental improvement. After renovation in the 1980s, Houhai, together with the surrounding green spaces and newly built attractions, became a recreational area for waterfront sightseeing, fishing, boating, and other activities.

西海又称积水潭，是什刹海后三海之一。现有资料将其放在高梁河水系、元大都漕运和什刹.en: Xihai, also known as Jishuitan, is one of the three rear seas of Shichahai. Existing materials discuss it within the history of the Gaoliang River water system, the grain-transport system of Dadu of the Yuan dynasty, and the improvement of Shichahai. An official historical text records that after renovation, the island of Huitong Temple was restored in Xihai; the temple was concealed among rocks, pines, and cypresses, while a two-story box-shaped hall inside the artificial hill was used as a cultural salon, serving functions including sightseeing, cultural entertainment, and traditional local snacks.

银锭桥是什刹海沿线的桥梁，并与“银锭观山”景观视廊相联系。官方报道描述，登桥可向.en: Yinding Bridge is a bridge along Shichahai and is associated with the “Yinding Mountain View” landscape corridor. Official reports state that from the bridge one can look west toward the Xishan peaks, with weeping willows and waterscapes visible nearby; “Yinding Mountain View” is listed as a strategic-level landscape corridor in the core area. The reports also state that lowering the height of the Jishuitan Hospital building restored the existing ridgeline view. Whether the mountains can be seen depends on weather and visibility.

德胜桥位于德胜门内大街、什刹海后海与西海交汇处，是一座闸桥合一的单孔石拱桥。西城.en: Desheng Bridge is located at the intersection of Deshengmennei Street, Shichahai Houhai, and Xihai. It is a single-span stone arch bridge combining a sluice and bridge. According to Xicheng District government materials, it was first built during the Ming dynasty, and its name derives from its proximity to Deshengmen. The bridge deck was originally arched; in 1919 it was changed to a relatively flatter deck and a pedestrian walkway was added. In 1943, the stone balustrades were replaced with brick-built parapets in the form of city walls. The above describes historical changes and does not represent current traffic conditions.

万宁桥（澄清上闸）位于中轴线、六海与元代通惠河的交界处，资料称其为大运河玉河故道.en: Wanning Bridge (Chengqing Upper Sluice) is located at the intersection of the central axis, the Six Seas, and the Tonghui River of the Yuan dynasty. Sources describe it as part of the former course of the Yu River of the Grand Canal and a Major Historical and Cultural Site Protected at the National Level. The Beijing Municipal Cultural Heritage Bureau records that the bridge was initially made of wood and later rebuilt in stone; it is a single-span arch bridge approximately 34.6 meters long and 17 meters wide. Chengqing Upper Sluice is located west of the bridge. Six water-suppressing beasts remain on both sides of the bridge, one on the northeastern revetment being explicitly identified as a Yuan-dynasty stone carving. Another source states that it was first built in the twenty-second year of the Zhiyuan era of the Yuan dynasty and records that its original name was restored after reconstruction in 2000.

万宁桥镇水兽是桥两侧现存的组合石刻记录。北京市文物局资料称桥西有四只、桥东有两只.en: The water-suppressing beasts at Wanning Bridge are a surviving group of stone carvings on both sides of the bridge. Materials from the Beijing Municipal Cultural Heritage Bureau state that there are four west of the bridge and two east of it, and that one on the northeastern revetment is a Yuan-dynasty stone carving. Beijing Tourism Net additionally records the inscription “ninth month of the fourth year of the Zhiyuan era” beneath its jaw. Related sources also preserve folk explanations involving water suppression and foretelling drought, but these accounts are traditional symbolism or former beliefs and cannot be used as descriptions of actual flood-control functions.

荷花市场位于什刹海前海西沿。资料称明清时期什刹海多植荷花，前海银锭桥以东尤盛；清.en: The Lotus Market is located along the western shore of Shichahai Qianhai. Sources state that many lotus flowers were planted in Shichahai during the Ming and Qing periods, especially east of Yinding Bridge in Qianhai. During the Tongzhi reign of the Qing dynasty, merchants were already setting up seats along the shore to sell tea, and the market formally acquired its name in the early Republican period. The market reopened in 1990 and displayed a plaque inscribed by Qigong. Current reports position it as a commercial district combining historical culture, urban memory, dining, daily life, cultural and creative products, and green ecology, but provide no continuing operating commitment for specific shops.

烟袋斜街位于西城区地安门外大街，资料称其最早形成于元代，清乾隆年间《日下旧闻考》.en: Yandai Xiejie is located outside Di’anmen Outer Street in Xicheng District. Sources state that it first took shape during the Yuan dynasty; the Qianlong-period work Rixia Jiuwen Kao records its former name as “Drum Tower Slanted Street,” and it was changed to its present name in the late Qing period. The street is approximately 232 meters long and is introduced as one of Beijing’s earliest slanted streets and a commercial pedestrian street with traditional cultural features. A route introduction by the Xicheng District government also mentions folk cultural content within the street, including paper-cutting, sugar figurine blowing, clay figurine making, traditional snacks, and hutong commemorative photography.

广福观位于烟袋斜街及大石碑胡同一带，明天顺三年（1459）由彭姓太监创建，清代曾.en: Guangfu Temple is located around Yandai Xiejie and Dashibei Hutong. It was founded by the eunuch Peng in the third year of the Tianshun era of the Ming dynasty (1459), renamed Fuyou Palace during the Qing dynasty, and restored to the name Guangfu Temple during the Republican period. After the founding of the People’s Republic of China, parts of it were converted into residences. The mountain gate, main hall, rear hall, and the main hall within Baiyun Xianyuan remain. It opened after restoration in 2008 and is now jointly used by the Shichahai Subdistrict and the Xicheng District Taoist Association, also serving as the Shichahai Cultural Exhibition Center. Related reports have recorded historical exhibitions and creative activities on the history of Shichahai held there.

敕建火德真君庙俗称火神庙，位于地安门外大街77号，是道教正一派道观，1984年列.en: The Imperially Established Temple of the True Lord Huode, commonly known as the Fire God Temple, is located at No. 77 Di’anmen Outer Street. It is a Zhengyi Taoist temple and was listed as a Beijing Municipal Cultural Heritage Site in 1984. District government materials state that it is traditionally said to have been first built in the sixth year of the Zhenguan era of the Tang dynasty (632), and rebuilt in the sixth year of the Zhizheng era of the Yuan dynasty. During the Wanli period of the Ming dynasty, after a fire in the Forbidden City, it was rebuilt on the Yuan-dynasty temple site and embellished with glazed tiles; further reconstruction took place during the Qing dynasty. The temple faces south, with its mountain gate facing east. The surviving structures include the mountain gate, bell and drum towers, and several halls. After clearance and restoration from 2001 to 2005, it was placed under the management and use of the China Taoist Association and opened to the public.

广化寺位于鸦儿胡同31号，始建于元代，明成化、万历及清代道光、咸丰、光绪年间多次.en: Guanghua Temple is located at No. 31 Ya’er Hutong. It was first built during the Yuan dynasty and repeatedly rebuilt during the Chenghua and Wanli periods of the Ming dynasty and the Daoguang, Xianfeng, and Guangxu periods of the Qing dynasty. The temple faces south, with its principal buildings arranged along the central axis, including a spirit wall, mountain-gate hall, Hall of the Heavenly Kings, Mahavira Hall, and Sutra Repository. On the west are courtyards containing the Guanyin Pavilion, Kṣitigarbha Pavilion, abbot’s quarters, Dharma hall, and ancestral hall; a two-storey hall remains on the eastern route, while the rest has been demolished or altered. Materials recorded in the Sutra Repository include the Ming edition of the Tripitaka, the Qianlong edition of the Pinqie Canon, and the Japanese edition of the Supplementary Canon. The temple also served at various times as the Jingshi Library, a Buddhist academy, and a primary school. In 1982, the Beijing Buddhist Association was established there.
广化寺位于鸦儿胡同31号，始建于元代，明成化、万历及清代道光、咸丰、光绪年间多次.revision: Codex依给定中文作专名、方位、混字及铭文转写的确定性校正；无新增模型调用

郭守敬纪念馆设于积水潭北岸的汇通祠内，相关资料称汇通祠始建于明永乐年间。2007.en: The Guo Shoujing Memorial Hall is located within Huitong Shrine on the northern bank of Jishuitan. Related sources state that Huitong Shrine was first built during the Yongle period of the Ming dynasty. From August 2007 to August 2008, the Xicheng District government restored the memorial hall and updated its exhibitions; after renovation, it opened free to the public on September 28, 2008. Cultural heritage bureau materials from 2025 describe it as covering nearly 800 square meters, with a building area of 400 square meters and four exhibition halls focusing respectively on Guo Shoujing’s life, Jishuitan during the Yuan dynasty, water control in Dadu, and astronomical observation and calendar making. Another official report from 2023 states that it has five exhibition halls, with different exhibition names and contents, reflecting exhibition information from different years.

西海湿地公园位于西海北岸一带，资料描述其由汇通祠石牌楼附近步道进入，可见开阔水面.en: Xihai Wetland Park is located along the northern shore of Xihai. Sources describe access by a path near the stone memorial archway of Huitong Shrine, with open water, reeds, waterbirds, and other wetland scenery visible. Reports associate the site with the northern terminus wharf of the Beijing–Hangzhou Grand Canal during the Yuan dynasty, noting that Xihai once witnessed the gathering of grain-transport vessels. A statue of Guo Shoujing stands by the shore, and nearby Huitong Shrine has been established as the Guo Shoujing Memorial Hall. Existing materials mainly describe the park’s shore environment, historical water-transport background, and cultural-display association; they do not provide an independent construction date, area, or opening arrangements.

郭守敬雕像位于西海湿地公园西海北岸，资料描述其设在岸边，塑造为元代水利专家郭守敬.en: The statue of Guo Shoujing is located on the northern shore of Xihai in Xihai Wetland Park. Sources describe it as standing by the shore and depicting the Yuan-dynasty hydraulic engineer Guo Shoujing holding a scroll and gazing ahead. Reports associate the statue with Guo Shoujing’s achievement of overseeing the construction of the Beijing–Hangzhou Grand Canal and mention that Huitong Shrine on the northern hillside has been established as the Guo Shoujing Memorial Hall. Existing sources confirm only the statue’s location, depiction, and commemorative significance; they do not state its creator, date of production, material, dimensions, or exact coordinates.

郭沫若纪念馆位于西城区前海西街，原为中西结合宅院，清末曾属于恭王府相关地产，民国.en: The Guo Moruo Memorial Hall is located on Qianhai West Street in Xicheng District. It was originally a residence combining Chinese and Western elements. In the late Qing period, it belonged to property associated with Prince Gong’s Residence; in the early Republican period, the Le family’s Daren Hall purchased the land and built the residence. After the founding of the People’s Republic of China, the residence was donated to the state and successively served as the Mongolian embassy in China and the residence of Soong Ching Ling. Guo Moruo moved in in November 1963, living and writing there and receiving members of the cultural community until his death in June 1978. The former residence opened to the public in 1988 and was renamed from “Guo Moruo Former Residence” to “Guo Moruo Memorial Hall” in 1994. Related sources also state that the furnishings from his lifetime, manuscripts, books, documentary materials, and personal belongings are preserved there.

宋庆龄故居位于西城区后海北沿46号，所在西花园原属醇亲王府，历史上先后被记为明珠.en: The Soong Ching Ling Former Residence is located at No. 46 along the northern shore of Houhai in Xicheng District. The Western Garden originally belonged to Prince Chun’s Residence and was historically recorded successively as the garden of Mingzhu’s residence, Heshen’s secondary residence, the garden of Prince Cheng’s Residence, and the garden of Prince Chun Zai Feng’s residence. Beijing municipal government materials state that Soong Ching Ling moved there in April 1963 and lived there until her death on May 29, 1981; it opened to the public on May 29, 1982. Xicheng District materials alternatively state that it was named “Former Residence of Comrade Soong Ching Ling, Honorary President of the People’s Republic of China” in October 1981 and opened to the public the following year.

醇亲王府（北府）位于后海北沿44号，原为明珠府，乾隆年间改为成亲王府，1888年.en: Prince Chun’s Residence (Northern Residence) is located at No. 44 along the northern shore of Houhai. It was originally the residence of Mingzhu, became Prince Cheng’s Residence during the Qianlong period, and was transferred to Prince Chun’s Residence in 1888. It was called the “Northern Residence” to distinguish it from the former residence on Baojia Street. The Xuantong Emperor Puyi of the Qing dynasty was born here, and his father Zai Feng was known as the regent. The residence faces south, with the residence compound in the east and a garden in the west. Sources list buildings including Yin’an Hall, Baohan Hall, Jiusi Hall, and Siqian Hall. The Western Garden was later converted into the Soong Ching Ling Former Residence.
醇亲王府（北府）位于后海北沿44号，原为明珠府，乾隆年间改为成亲王府，1888年.revision: Codex依给定中文作专名、方位、混字及铭文转写的确定性校正；无新增模型调用

庆王府位于定阜街3号，原为道光时期大学士琦善宅第，后因籍没而赐予奕劻。来源一记咸.en: Prince Qing’s Residence is located at No. 3 Dingfu Street. It was originally the residence of Qishan, a grand secretary during the Daoguang period, and was later confiscated and bestowed on Yikuang. One source dates the bestowal to the first year of the Xianfeng era (1851), while another gives 1841; regarding the date of rebuilding or ennoblement, the former records rebuilding in the tenth year of the Guangxu era (1884), while the latter records ennoblement as Prince Qing in the twentieth year of the Guangxu era (1894). The buildings are divided into principal halls and eastern and western living areas. Existing materials particularly describe three groups of courtyards and numerous halls in the western section, as well as a number of two-story embroidered towers.

涛贝勒府位于柳荫街27号，涛贝勒载涛为醇贤亲王奕譞第七子、摄政王载沣之弟。府址原.en: Beile Zaitao’s Residence is located at No. 27 Liuyin Street. Beile Zaitao was the seventh son of Prince Chun Xian Yixuan and the younger brother of the regent Zai Feng. The site was originally the residence of Yinyu, the fifteenth son of the Kangxi Emperor, and was converted into Zai Tao’s residence in the late Qing period. The residence faces south, with the residential compound in the north and a garden in the south. The compound was divided into central, eastern, and western routes; the garden had a covered corridor, pavilions, a flower hall, rockeries, and stables. In 1925 it was rented to the Holy See as the site of Fu Jen University, and part of the residence later became Fu Jen Boys’ Middle School. In 1952, related courtyards were leveled to build teaching buildings and sports grounds; some courtyards on the central and eastern routes still retain the character of a princely residence.
涛贝勒府位于柳荫街27号，涛贝勒载涛为醇贤亲王奕譞第七子、摄政王载沣之弟。府址原.revision: Codex依给定中文作专名、方位、混字及铭文转写的确定性校正；无新增模型调用

辅仁大学旧址（定阜街主楼）位于定阜街1号，所在地原为涛贝勒府花园和马厩。1925.en: The Former Site of Fu Jen University (Main Building on Dingfu Street) is located at No. 1 Dingfu Street. The site originally comprised the garden and stables of Beile Zaitao’s Residence. In 1925, Zai Tao rented it to the Holy See, and Fu Jen University was founded by the American Catholic Benedictines. In 1930, a Chinese-Western-style main teaching building was completed on the vacant land and at the stables. The building once contained classrooms, laboratories, a library, offices, and an auditorium accommodating 1,000 people. In 1952, Fu Jen University merged with Beijing Normal University, and the main building became the premises of the chemistry department of Beijing Normal University.

会贤堂旧址位于前海北沿18号，曾为北京八大堂之一。其前身是清光绪时期礼部侍郎斌儒.en: The Former Site of Huixian Hall is located at No. 18 along the northern shore of Qianhai and was once one of Beijing’s Eight Great Halls. Its predecessor was the private residence of Bin Ru, a vice minister of the Ministry of Rites during the Guangxu period of the Qing dynasty. In 1890, a native of Jinan, Shandong, opened the Huixian Hall restaurant there. The multi-story building facing the street offered views of Shichahai; the door ornaments bore the inscription “All the Worthies Have Gathered.” The rear courtyard was divided into eastern and western routes and contained multiple rooms, a garden, and a theater stage. It was once a gathering place for literati, officials, and nobles. Sources record that the restaurant ceased operations in the 1940s and was purchased by Fu Jen University in 1948 for use as an alumni building.

关岳庙位于鼓楼西大街149号，原为醇贤亲王庙，始建于光绪十七年（1891），光绪.en: Guanyue Temple is located at No. 149 Gulou West Street. It was originally the temple of Prince Chun Xian and was first built in the seventeenth year of the Guangxu era (1891), completed in the twenty-fifth year of the Guangxu era (1899). The temple faces south. Along the central axis are a spirit wall, central gate, main hall, and rear shrine, with additional structures including a divine kitchen, divine storehouse, sacrificial-animal pavilion, and well pavilion. In 1914, the Beiyang government installed statues of Guan Yu and Yue Fei in the rear shrine, and it consequently also became known as the Martial Temple. After 1949, the site served as the Beijing office of the Dalai Lama of Tibet.

鸦儿胡同属西城区什刹海街道，东南起小石碑胡同并与烟袋斜街相连，西北至甘露胡同。其.en: Ya’er Hutong belongs to Shichahai Subdistrict, Xicheng District. It begins in the southeast at Xiaoshibei Hutong, connects with Yandai Xiejie, and extends northwest to Ganlu Hutong. Its name history includes “Yan’er Hutong” in the Yuan dynasty and “Guanghua Temple Street” in the Ming dynasty; in the Qing dynasty, the names “Ya’er Hutong” and “Yā’er Hutong” developed through phonetic similarity. The hutong is 820 meters long, with Guanghua Temple, the Soong Ching Ling Former Residence, and Xiao Jun’s former residence “Wowo Residence” among the heritage sites and former residences of notable figures along it. Sources also record that after commercial development around Houhai, some houses were converted into bars and the environment and functions of the lanes changed.
鸦儿胡同属西城区什刹海街道，东南起小石碑胡同并与烟袋斜街相连，西北至甘露胡同。其.revision: Codex依给定中文作专名、方位、混字及铭文转写的确定性校正；无新增模型调用

德胜门箭楼位于西城区德胜门立交桥北侧，是明清北京内城九座城门之一。来源记载其建成.en: The Deshengmen Arrow Tower is located north of the Deshengmen overpass in Xicheng District and is one of the nine gates of the inner city of Beijing during the Ming and Qing periods. Sources record that it was completed in 1439 and subsequently underwent construction and repair to varying degrees. The arrow tower faces north, has an inverted stepped and projecting plan, seven bays in width and two bays in depth, and uses a front-tower/rear-extension layout. It has a double-eaved hip-and-gable roof with green-glazed tile edging. Materials list it as a Ming-Qing city-defense facility and as physical material for studying ancient capital construction, architectural building techniques, and the history of Beijing’s urban development.
德胜门箭楼位于西城区德胜门立交桥北侧，是明清北京内城九座城门之一。来源记载其建成.revision: Codex依给定中文作专名、方位、混字及铭文转写的确定性校正；无新增模型调用

梅兰芳纪念馆原为梅兰芳故居，位于护国寺街9号。旧文称梅兰芳自1950年迁入后一直.en: The Mei Lanfang Memorial Hall was originally Mei Lanfang’s former residence and is located at No. 9 Huguosi Street. Earlier texts state that Mei Lanfang moved in in 1950 and lived there until his death; the former residence is a Beijing courtyard house facing south, with a small sitting room, the study “Zhuiyu Studio,” and living quarters. Materials from the Beijing Municipal Cultural Heritage Bureau state that after Mei Lanfang’s death, his family donated a large quantity of opera materials and documents to the state. The memorial hall began preparations in 1984, officially opened in 1986, and houses related materials. Two official sources differ in their accounts of the period of residence.

恭王府及花园位于什刹海西南角，由府邸和花园两部分组成。府邸分东、中、西三路，各路.en: Prince Gong’s Residence and Garden is located at the southwestern corner of Shichahai and consists of a residence compound and a garden. The residence is divided into eastern, central, and western routes, each organized around a central axis with multiple successive courtyard houses. The garden is likewise divided into three routes and contains such features as a Western-style gate, the Stele of the “Fu” Character, Dule Peak, and Bat Pool. Sources state that it was first built in the late Qianlong period of the Qing dynasty and successively served as Heshen’s residence, Prince Qing’s Residence, and Prince Gong’s Residence. Its layout and forms combine official architecture with residential characteristics. The rear covered building and Xijin Studio are both described in different official introductions, but the length of the rear covered building is recorded variously as 156 meters and 189 meters.

北京钟鼓楼是位于北京南北中轴线北端的古代建筑群，两楼前后纵向排列，曾承担元、明、.en: The Beijing Bell and Drum Towers are an ancient architectural complex at the northern end of Beijing’s north-south central axis. The two towers are arranged longitudinally, one behind the other, and once served the timekeeping function of the capital during the Yuan, Ming, and Qing dynasties. According to sources, the surviving Bell Tower was completed in 1747 during the Qianlong period of the Qing dynasty. It is 47.9 meters high overall, built of brick and stone, and houses a time-telling bronze bell cast during the Yongle period of the Ming dynasty. The Drum Tower is 46.7 meters high overall, originally named Qizheng Tower, and underwent reconstruction during the Yuan and Ming periods as well as rebuilding and repairs during the Qing dynasty. Of the original time drums, only one main drum remains; 25 replica time drums are also displayed.

北京鼓楼初名齐政楼，始建于元至元九年（1272），后因火灾重建，明永乐十八年（1.en: Beijing Drum Tower was originally named Qizheng Tower. It was first built in the ninth year of the Zhiyuan era of the Yuan dynasty (1272), rebuilt after a fire, rebuilt again in the eighteenth year of the Yongle era of the Ming dynasty (1420), and reportedly rebuilt again during the Qing dynasty. The surviving building is 46.7 meters high overall and is a timber pavilion with triple eaves and three levels of dripping water. The lower level is a brick-and-stone structure with arched vaults and no beams; the upper level is a brick-and-timber structure. It is five bays wide and three bays deep, with a surrounding corridor. The Drum Tower once served to announce the watches. Of the original 25 time drums, only one main drum remains, while 25 replica time drums are displayed.

北京钟楼是钟鼓楼建筑群中的钟楼，历史上始建于元至元九年（1272），1297年复.en: The Beijing Bell Tower is the bell tower within the Bell and Drum Towers complex. Historically, it was first built in the ninth year of the Zhiyuan era of the Yuan dynasty (1272), rebuilt in 1297, rebuilt again in the eighteenth year of the Yongle era of the Ming dynasty (1420), and rebuilt once more during the Qing dynasty. The Capital Window source states that the surviving building was completed in 1747 during the Qianlong period of the Qing dynasty. The Beijing Municipal Cultural Heritage Bureau records reconstruction in the tenth year of the Qianlong era (1745) and explains that an associated stele records the project in the twelfth year of the Qianlong era (1747). The Bell Tower is 47.9 meters high overall, built of brick and stone, with a double-eaved hip-and-gable roof; its interior contains cross-shaped vaults and a courtyard well.

钟楼明永乐报时铜钟悬挂于北京钟楼上层，来源称其铸造于明永乐年间，并刻有“永乐年、.en: The Ming Yongle time-telling bronze bell in the Bell Tower hangs in the upper level of the Beijing Bell Tower. Sources state that it was cast during the Yongle period of the Ming dynasty and bears the inscription “Cast on an auspicious day of the year and month of Yongle.” The bell is 7.02 meters high overall, has a maximum diameter of 3.4 meters, and weighs approximately 63 tons. Sources also record that the Bell Tower uses its courtyard well and cross-shaped vaults to form vertically overlapping resonant chambers, and that historically the bell was struck 108 times at each watch. This bronze bell is a time-telling object within the Bell Tower and is not the Bell Tower building itself.

鼓楼残存主鼓与复制更鼓陈列，是北京鼓楼二层报时器具遗存与展示组合。官方资料称，鼓.en: The surviving main drum and displayed replica time drums constitute a combination of surviving timekeeping implements and exhibition objects on the second floor of Beijing Drum Tower. Official materials state that the Drum Tower originally had 25 time drums, of which only one main drum survives; 25 replica time drums are currently displayed. Accordingly, the surviving main drum and the other replica drums differ in nature, and all 25 cannot be regarded as Ming-Qing originals. Related records also state that the main drum and group of drums were used to announce the watches at the Drum Tower, with 108 drumbeats sounded each night historically.

萧军故居“蜗蜗居”位于鸦儿胡同6号院内，是一座木构西式二层小楼。官方资料称，萧军.en: Xiao Jun’s Former Residence “Wowo Residence” is located within the compound at No. 6 Ya’er Hutong and is a small two-story Western-style timber building. Official materials state that Xiao Jun lived there from 1951 until his death. During this period he wrote works including The Mine in May, Historical Stories of the Spring and Autumn Periods of Wu and Yue, and The Third Generation, as well as several collections of letters; he also suffered persecution during the Cultural Revolution. The site is listed as a Beijing Municipal Cultural Heritage Site. An older official text also records that the building had been emptied by early 2005.

恭王府花园又称萃锦园，属于恭王府的花园部分，与府邸相对独立。官方资料称，花园占地.en: The Garden of Prince Gong’s Residence, also known as Cuijin Garden, is the garden section of Prince Gong’s Residence and is relatively independent from the residence compound. Official materials state that the garden covers approximately 28,860 square meters and is divided into eastern, central, and western routes. The central route enters through a white-marble Western-style arched stone gate and centers on the Stele of the “Fu” Character inscribed by the Kangxi Emperor. Dule Peak and Bat Pool are in front, while Lütian Xiaoyin and the Bat Hall are behind, forming a richly layered garden layout. The garden’s name is also written in sources as “Langrun Garden or Cuijin Garden.”

怡神所即大戏楼，位于恭王府花园东路，因楼内曾悬挂康熙御笔“怡神所”匾额而得名。官.en: Yishensuo, namely the Grand Theater, is located on the eastern route of the garden of Prince Gong’s Residence. It was named after the plaque inscribed “Yishensuo” in the Kangxi Emperor’s handwriting that once hung inside. Official materials state that the building faces south, covers 722 square meters, and is a fully enclosed timber structure with three linked volumes and hooked connections. Inside are a stage, audience seating, and boxes in the north. Furnishings include the plaque “Pleasant Things for the Heart,” palace lanterns, Qing-style furniture, and wisteria decoration; its architectural, acoustic, and aesthetic designs each have distinctive characteristics.

福字碑位于恭王府花园滴翠岩下的秘云洞内。官方资料称，碑身长129厘米、宽54厘米.en: The Stele of the “Fu” Character is located inside Miyun Cave beneath Dicui Rock in the garden of Prince Gong’s Residence. Official materials state that the stele is 129 centimeters long and 54 centimeters wide. At the center of its face is the character “Fu,” with character dimensions of 59 by 33 centimeters; above it is the seal inscription “Treasure of the Kangxi Emperor’s Imperial Brush.” Sources interpret the character’s form as incorporating the images of “zi (children),” “cai (talent),” “shou (longevity),” and “tian (fields),” symbolizing many children, talents, fields, longevity, and blessings.

The outer side of the gate lintel is carved with “Jing han tai gu,” and the inner side with “Xiu yi heng chun.” The line-method walls on both sides of the gate also bear finely executed reliefs, demonstrating a combination of Western forms and local cultural decoration.

后罩楼位于恭王府府邸与花园的分界处，是横贯东西的二层建筑。官方资料称，其东西长约.en: The Rear Cover Building is located at the boundary between the residence and garden of Prince Gong’s Mansion and is a two-story building extending from east to west. Official sources state that it is approximately 151 meters long from east to west and 25 meters wide from north to south, with 116 rooms, commonly known as “99 and a half rooms.” Its eastern, central, and western sections are respectively named Zhanji Tower, Fujing Tower, and Baoyue Tower. Passages to the rear garden are located on both sides of the central section. At the westernmost end, there was once an indoor garden called the Waterworks Building, containing flowing springs, rockeries, and pavilions; remains of the indoor garden survive.

银安殿是恭王府中路正殿，面阔五间，覆绿色琉璃瓦，前有月台及东西对称的抄手台阶、灯.en: Yin’an Hall is the main hall on the central axis of Prince Gong’s Mansion. It is five bays wide and covered with green glazed tiles. In front are a moon platform, symmetrical stepped side approaches to the east and west, and lamp columns; subsidiary halls stand on both sides of the platform. The official website states that it was first built during the period of the Gurun Princess. The original building and the eastern and western subsidiary halls were destroyed by fire on the night of the Lantern Festival in 1920. The present buildings were reconstructed in 2008 according to the layout of the period of Prince Gong. The original text also records that the hall originally contained the prince’s throne and was used for ceremonies, rituals, governmental affairs, and sacrificial activities at the residence.

嘉乐堂位于恭王府府邸中路第四进院落，是银安殿后的寝殿，也是中路最后一间正厅。正殿.en: Jiale Hall is located in the fourth courtyard of the central axis of the residence of Prince Gong’s Mansion. It is the bedchamber behind Yin’an Hall and the last main hall on the central axis. The main hall is five bays wide, with a flush-gable roof and a front corridor, and is covered with green glazed tiles; subsidiary halls are located to the east and west. The official website states that it was first built during the period of the Gurun Princess and was originally a place for Shamanist sacrificial ceremonies, hence its other name, “Divine Hall.” The hall once contained a stove, a large cauldron, and a “wanzi kang,” used for cooking sacrificial offerings and distributing the food after the rituals. The eastern subsidiary hall once stored ritual vessels, while the western subsidiary hall once housed sacrificial livestock. Remains related to the rituals are also preserved in the courtyard.

葆光室位于恭王府府邸西路第三进院落，院落规模较小，正殿五间，东西耳房各三间。官网.en: Baoguang Room is located in the third courtyard of the western section of the residence of Prince Gong’s Mansion. The courtyard is relatively small, with a five-bay main hall and three side rooms on each of the east and west sides. The official website states that it was first built during the period of the Princess’s Residence, and that Heshen once entertained close relatives and friends here. During the period of Prince Gong, the Xianfeng Emperor bestowed the name “Baoguang Room” and explained its meaning as “concealing one’s brilliance and not letting others know,” carrying an admonition for Yixin to restrain his talents and abilities. After Yixin died of illness in 1898, Empress Dowager Cixi and the Guangxu Emperor discussed and settled various funeral arrangements with relevant ministers here.

锡晋斋位于恭王府府邸西路第四进院落，始建于公主府时期。官网称其在庆王时期名为“庆.en: Xijin Studio is located in the fourth courtyard of the western section of the residence of Prince Gong’s Mansion and was first built during the period of the Princess’s Residence. The official website states that during the period of Prince Qing it was called Qingyi Hall; during the period of the Junior Prince Gong, Puwei, it was renamed with its present name because it housed the Jin-dynasty Lu Ji’s handwritten copy of the “Pingfu Tie.” The main hall is seven bays wide, with corridors at the front and rear and a hip-and-gable-roofed baoxia at the rear eaves. Inside are a three-bay open hall and three-sided, two-story “immortal towers.” Components of golden-thread nanmu, nanmu partitions, and polychrome painted ceilings were used, and the layout is said to imitate the Palace of Tranquil Longevity. The eastern and western side rooms are respectively Legu Studio and Er’er Studio.

多福轩位于恭王府府邸东路第三进院落，正殿五间，覆灰色筒瓦，东西各有耳房。殿内悬有.en: Duofu Studio is located in the third courtyard of the eastern section of the residence of Prince Gong’s Mansion. The main hall is five bays wide and covered with gray tubular tiles, with side rooms to the east and west. Inside the hall hangs a plaque reading “Tong de yan xi,” bestowed by Empress Dowager Cixi for Prince Gong Yixin’s fiftieth birthday. Square calligraphic panels bearing the characters “fu (blessings)” and “shou (longevity)” are displayed above the four walls, and a large nanmu bookcase is set against the north wall. The painted ceiling features magnolias and crabapple blossoms. The official website states that remnants of Qianlong-period phoenix-and-seal polychrome painting remain on the beams. A wisteria over one hundred years old stands in the courtyard in front of the hall, and the courtyard is therefore also called the “Wisteria Courtyard.”

乐道堂位于恭王府府邸东路第四进院落。正殿北卷明间脊檩绘有反搭包袱凤和玺彩画，主图.en: Ledaotang is located in the fourth courtyard of the eastern section of the residence of Prince Gong’s Mansion. On the ridge purlin of the central bay of the northern roll-roofed section of the main hall are reverse-mounted baofu phoenix-and-seal polychrome paintings; the principal motifs are a spreading-winged golden phoenix, peonies, and auspicious clouds. The official website states that after the Gurun Heke Princess married, she lived in this courtyard for ten years, when it was called Yanxi Hall. In the thirtieth year of the Daoguang reign, after Yixin was granted Prince Qing’s Mansion, he renamed it Ledaotang. “Ledaotang” is said to have been inscribed by the Daoguang Emperor for Yixin before his wedding; he also bestowed a plaque and couplets expressing good wishes. Yixin later used this name for the main halls of several of his residences.

The official website states that it is nearly 200 meters long. In addition to serving as a daily passageway, it was historically used by the prince and his sons and younger male relatives for practicing horseback riding and archery. The sources provided mainly describe its location, material, dimensions, and historical use, without further information on surviving features along the roadway, its construction date, or its architectural structure.

It is an approximately five-meter-high solitary ornamental rock of northern Taihu stone. The official website states that it was placed near the garden entrance both to embellish the landscape and block the view, while also serving as a screen wall and screen. Natural textures formed through years of weathering cover the stone; the original text compares its form to a whirlpool in soft water or thin clouds unfurling. When viewed from below, the two characters “Le Feng” can be seen, while the character “Du” is hidden at the top of the stone, creating a visual play on its name.

蝠池位于恭王府花园中路独乐峰北侧，是一方以青石围砌的水池。其旧名为“蝠河”，后改.en: The Bat Pond is located in the central section of the garden of Prince Gong’s Mansion, north of Dule Peak. It is a pond enclosed with bluestone. Its former name was the “Bat River,” later changed to “Bat Pond”; the name derives from the pond’s resemblance to a bat. Elm trees grow beside the pond. In late spring, elm samaras fall into the pond, and because they resemble copper coins, they were imbued with the auspicious meaning of “an abundance of blessings and wealth,” expressing the wish for both good fortune and prosperity.

It was named after the plaque inscribed by the Xianfeng Emperor in his own hand with “Dihua Xuan.” The official website connects its name with the experiences of Yizhu and Yixin practicing spear and saber techniques in their youth: the Daoguang Emperor bestowed the name “Dihua United Effort” on the spear technique and “Treasure Edge Proclaiming Might” on the saber technique, expressing his hope that the brothers would work together. The sources thus present the courtly familial implications carried by the name Dihua Studio.

安善堂位于恭王府花园中路，是一座五开间厅堂。其主体为两卷勾连搭歇山顶建筑，南侧设.en: Anshan Hall is located in the central section of the garden of Prince Gong’s Mansion and is a five-bay hall. Its main structure consists of a building with two linked hip-and-gable-roofed sections; a three-bay flush-gable-roofed baoxia is attached to the south, and covered walkways connect the east and west sides. The name derives from a plaque inscribed by the Xianfeng Emperor in his own hand. In terms of historical use, it was originally a place where the owner composed poetry and painted while visiting the garden; during the period of Prince Gong Yixin, it was also used to entertain important guests.

滴翠岩是一座以太湖石叠成的假山，位于恭王府花园中路安善堂北边；秘云洞藏在假山腹部.en: Dicui Rock is an artificial hill formed by stacking Taihu stones, located north of Anshan Hall in the central section of the garden of Prince Gong’s Mansion. The top of Dicui Rock is the highest point in the garden, with the “Green Heaven Little Hermitage” and Moon-Inviting Terrace located there. According to the official website, the name is related to moss among the rocks: in the past, after water was stored, emerald-green moss grew on the rock walls in summer and autumn, forming a scene of yellow stone and green moss, lush and dripping with verdure.
